=== DELIVERABLE 1 — Narrowed Novelty Claims (Action #26, §2.3) — FINAL ===

**Claim 1** (proposed, Track 1, task_2026-08-21_002):
"SPARK's Layer 1/Layer 2 pipeline combines a continuously-sampled software magnitude-and-duration threshold gate with a subsequent quantized CNN confirmation, both executing entirely on a single commodity MCU (ESP32-S3) with no offload to a gateway or server for the classification decision — a combination not found together in the reviewed 2023-2026 literature, where comparable systems either run the confirmation model on a server/gateway (Xu et al., 2021), run a single always-on MCU-resident CNN without a preceding gate (Yu et al., 2023; Hu et al., 2025), gate via the IMU's native low-power interrupt hardware rather than a continuous software threshold (Sensors, 2025), or achieve genuine same-chip two-stage inference only at FPGA/RISC-V SoC hardware tiers well above a $5-class MCU (IEEE Xplore, 2024)."
Pre-thesis-submission actions flagged by Track 1: (a) resolve a MicroFallNet name-collision — two sources with this exact title report different datasets/MCUs (ESP32 vs ESP32-S3), unclear if same paper cited inconsistently or two papers; (b) pull Xu et al. 2021 full text directly (currently abstract/secondary-source only, paywalled); (c) this pass used general web search proxying IEEE Xplore/ScienceDirect/MDPI, not a direct Boolean DB query — Action #26 asked for the latter; treat as strong first pass, not fully "formal" yet.

**Claim 3** (proposed, Track 2, task_2026-08-21_003):
"SPARK computes per-event fall explanations using gradient×input (DeepSHAP-equivalent) saliency attribution over the raw IMU window, executed on a local, non-cloud laptop gateway (with optional NPU/iGPU acceleration) rather than on the MCU-class wearable itself or via a cloud SHAP API — a combination of (a) a computationally lightweight gradient-based attribution method suited to real-time per-event use on resource-constrained infrastructure, (b) execution at a distinct local companion-device gateway rather than on-wearable or cloud compute, and (c) fall-specific clinical delivery, that is not jointly demonstrated in the closest identified prior art."
Closest prior art to cite in related-work: Liu et al. (IEEE ISCT 2024), Arul et al. (IEEE SCES 2024), Guo & Nakayama (Sensors 2025, 25(20):6500 — closest single-paper analog, differs on model type/offline-vs-runtime/no separate gateway). Track 2 flags the "local non-cloud gateway" framing as the load-bearing gap — recommends 2-3 direct IEEE Xplore/ACM DL UI searches before finalizing, since this pass used web search proxying those databases, not direct queries.

**Claim 4** — caution note, not a rewrite (Track 3, task_2026-08-21_004):
The narrow mechanism (config-file runtime override, no firmware reflash, MCU-class hardware) still has no direct prior art hit and needs no wording change. But the BROADER concept of adjustable/personalized fall-detection thresholds is real prior art: US Patent 8,217,795 B2 (priority 2006, granted 2012 — adjustable α/β thresholds tunable by "qualified professionals," no hardware change); a newer US patent application on probability-distribution-derived personalized thresholds; and Naranjo-Hernandez et al., IEEE Trans. Inf. Technol. Biomed. 16(2):264-271, 2012 (seen only via secondary citation — verify primary source before citing in thesis). Action: never state or imply "no existing system allows adjustable/personalized fall-detection sensitivity" anywhere in the thesis — that is false and prior art since at least 2007. Keep Claim 4 precisely scoped to the config-file/no-reflash/MCU-class combination.

**Claims 2 & 5**: Track 3 re-verified, both still hold, no wording change needed.
- Claim 2 (Nepal-context dataset): no South Asian/Nepal-context fall-detection dataset paper found 2025-2026 across multiple search angles; regional surveys (India, Bangladesh) note the gap but don't fill it.
- Claim 5 (local SHAP-annotated PDF report): closest prior art is cloud-based, non-explainable institutional incident-report patents (assisted-living-facility context) — architecturally different (cloud vs local, no SHAP content). Keep "local/offline" AND "SHAP-annotated" both explicit in the claim wording — drop either qualifier and it drifts into existing patent territory.

=== DELIVERABLE 2 — Data Collection Protocol Completion — NOW COMPLETE (was flagged incomplete in prior checkpoint) ===

Source: Track 7 (task_2026-08-21_008), verified against Sucerquia et al. 2017 (Sensors 17(1):198, DOI 10.3390/s17010198), Table 1/2, primary source.

Mapping method: SPARK's existing F01-F08/D01-D14 are reworded/reordered SisFall analogs, not verbatim copies. Mapping them to SisFall's 15 fall types + 19 ADL types leaves exactly 7 unused fall types and 7 unused ADL-candidates (for 5 slots) — F07 (table-assisted fall) is excluded on safety grounds, same logic SisFall itself used to exclude stair-falls ("high risk of having an accident").

**F09-F15 rows (insert into docs/DATA_COLLECTION_PROTOCOL.md in existing table format):**
| Code | Description | Protocol |
|---|---|---|
| F09 | Forward fall while jogging (trip) | Jog 3-4 paces on approach at a reduced/controlled pace, simulate tripping on obstacle, fall forward onto hands/mat. |
| F10 | Lateral fall when trying to get up | From seated position on chair, begin rising, lose lateral balance mid-rise, fall onto left/right flank onto adjacent mat. |
| F11 | Forward fall when trying to sit down | Approach chair from front, misjudge seat position while lowering, pitch forward and fall onto hands/mat instead of sitting. |
| F12 | Lateral fall when trying to sit down | Approach chair, lose lateral balance while lowering to seat, fall onto left/right flank onto mat beside chair. |
| F13 | Forward fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, pitch forward off chair onto mat. |
| F14 | Backward fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, fall backward off chair onto mat. |
| F15 | Lateral fall while seated (fainting/drowsiness) | Seated in chair, simulate sudden fainting/falling asleep, fall to left/right side off chair onto mat. |

**D15-D19 rows:**
| Code | Description | Reps |
|---|---|---|
| D15 | Bending at the waist without bending knees (straight-leg forward bend), then standing | 5 repetitions |
| D16 | Getting into a car/taxi, remaining seated briefly, then getting out | 5 repetitions |
| D17 | Gentle jump without falling (e.g. reaching a high object) | 5 repetitions |
| D18 | Sitting, attempting to rise, and collapsing back into the chair (near-fall, no actual fall) | 5 repetitions |
| D19 | Lying down slowly onto a mat/bed, pausing, then sitting up again | 5 repetitions |

Confidence split (per Track 7): D16/D17/D19 (mapped to SisFall D16, D17, D19) are high-confidence, low-ambiguity picks — D16 isolates a distinct trunk-flexion technique SPARK's existing D08 doesn't test and is specifically called out in SisFall's own methodology as a strong false-positive-similarity ADL; D17 is Nepal-relevant (public transport) and stress-tests Layer 1's |a|>2.5g gate (R-01); D19 adds a vertical-acceleration spike distinct from existing D09. D18/D19-as-numbered-here (mapped to SisFall D11/D12) are the LOWER-confidence judgment-call picks — presented as best-available default, explicitly pending Aaradhya's sign-off, not settled. Double-checked for duplication: SisFall F11 ("backward fall trying to sit down") is already SPARK's existing F04, correctly excluded from the new rows.

Track 7's own recommendation: do not mechanically append SisFall's raw F09-F15/D15-D19 — each row was checked against what SPARK already covers under different wording first, to avoid duplicate mechanisms. This has been done; the rows above are ready to insert as-is, with the D18/D19 caveat noted.
